title: Quietly Simmered Greek White Beans Saganaki
description: A romantic Greek dish featuring dried white beans, slow-cooked to perfection in a scallop shell, with a grassy and aerated texture, friendly to ayurvedic-rajasic diets. This recipe is a unique twist on traditional Greek cuisine.

ingredients.name: dried white beans
ingredients.notes: such as navy or cannellini beans

instructions: Rinse the dried white beans and soak them in water for at least 8 hours or overnight.
Drain and rinse the soaked beans, then transfer them to a large pot with enough water to cover them.
Bring the water to a boil, then reduce the heat to a simmer and cook the beans for 45 minutes, or until they are tender.
Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat, then add the chopped onion and cook until it is translucent.
Add the minced garlic to the skillet and cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly to prevent burning.
Stir in the tomato paste, lemon juice, dried oregano, and fresh thyme, then cook for 2 minutes.
Add the cooked white beans to the skillet and stir to combine with the tomato paste mixture.
Season the beans with salt and pepper to taste, then simmer them for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Spoon the bean mixture into the scallop shells, then top each shell with crumbled feta cheese.
Serve the Quietly Simmered Greek White Beans Saganaki hot, garnished with fresh herbs if desired.
